title: Deuteronomy Chapter 32 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 32 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 32 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 32.

questions.question: To whom does Moses say he will speak in Deuteronomy 32:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Heavens and earth
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:1 states, "Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth."

questions.question: How does Moses describe his doctrine in Deuteronomy 32:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Like the rain and dew
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:2 says, "My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew..."

questions.question: Why does Moses say he will publish the name of the LORD in Deuteronomy 32:3?
questions.correctAnswer: To ascribe greatness to God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:3 states, "Because I will publish the name of the LORD: ascribe ye greatness unto our God."

questions.question: How is God described in Deuteronomy 32:4?
options: The Rock, perfect in work, just and right
questions.correctAnswer: The Rock, perfect in work, just and right
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:4 describes God as "the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he."

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:5, how are the people described?
questions.correctAnswer: Perversion and crooked generation
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:5 says, "They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation."

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 32:6 calls the people foolish and unwise for their treatment of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:6 states, "Do ye thus requite the LORD, O foolish people and unwise?" showing the foolishness of their actions.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 32:7, Moses instructs to remember the days of old by asking whom?
questions.correctAnswer: Father and elders
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:7 says to "ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee."

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 32:8, the Most High set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:8 states, "he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

questions.question: Who is described as the LORD's portion and inheritance in Deuteronomy 32:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:9 says, "For the LORD'S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance."

questions.question: What action did the LORD take for his people in the desert according to Deuteronomy 32:10?
options: He led, instructed, and kept them as the apple of his eye
questions.correctAnswer: He led, instructed, and kept them as the apple of his eye
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:10 states, "He found him in a desert land... he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye."

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 32:12 states that the LORD led the people with many strange gods alongside Him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:12 says, "So the LORD alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him."

questions.question: What did God cause His people to suck out of the rock according to Deuteronomy 32:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Honey and oil
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:13 says, "...and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock;"

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as part of the blessings in Deuteronomy 32:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold and silver
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:14 lists butter, milk, fat of lambs, rams of Bashan, goats, wheat, and grape wine but does not mention gold or silver.

questions.question: What did Jeshurun do after growing fat according to Deuteronomy 32:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Forsook God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:15 states, "then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation."

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 32:18 says that the people remembered the Rock that begat them and honored God that formed them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:18 states, "Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee."

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 32 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 32 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:19, why did the LORD abhor his people?
options: Because of their wealth and pride
Because of the provoking of his sons and daughters
Because they worshiped the true God
Because they were obedient and humble
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the provoking of his sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:19 states that the LORD abhorred them because of the provoking of his sons and daughters, indicating their disobedience and turning away from God.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 32:20 say about the generation that provokes the LORD?
options: They are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith
questions.correctAnswer: They are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith
questions.explanation: Verse 20 describes the generation as 'very froward' and lacking faith, which explains why God said He would hide His face from them.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:21 describe God's response to Israel's idolatry?
options: He will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people
questions.correctAnswer: He will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explains that God will provoke Israel to jealousy by using a foolish nation, as a consequence of their idolatry and provocation.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 32:22 uses the imagery of fire to describe God's anger. What will this fire do?
options: Warm the earth and bring rain
Burn unto the lowest hell and consume the earth with her increase
questions.correctAnswer: Burn unto the lowest hell and consume the earth with her increase
questions.explanation: Verse 22 uses vivid imagery of a consuming fire kindled in God's anger that will burn to the lowest hell and consume the earth and mountains' foundations.

questions.question: What kinds of calamities does God promise to bring upon the people in Deuteronomy 32:23-24?
options: Mischiefs, arrows, hunger, burning heat, destruction, beasts, and serpents
questions.correctAnswer: Mischiefs, arrows, hunger, burning heat, destruction, beasts, and serpents
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 detail the severe calamities including mischiefs, arrows, hunger, heat, destruction, and attacks by beasts and serpents as judgment for their disobedience.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:25, who will be destroyed by the sword and terror?
options: Young men and virgins, sucklings and men of gray hairs
questions.correctAnswer: Young men and virgins, sucklings and men of gray hairs
questions.explanation: Verse 25 explicitly states that both the young and old, male and female, will be destroyed by sword and terror, showing the totality of the judgment.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:26-27 explain why God does not completely obliterate His people?
options: Because God fears the wrath of their enemies and their boasting
questions.correctAnswer: Because God fears the wrath of their enemies and their boasting
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 indicate that God restrains complete destruction to avoid giving enemies cause to say their own power, not God, caused Israel's downfall.

questions.question: What is said about the nation in Deuteronomy 32:28?
options: They are full of wisdom and understanding
They are a nation void of counsel and understanding
They are a holy and chosen people
questions.correctAnswer: They are a nation void of counsel and understanding
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clearly describes the nation as lacking counsel and understanding, highlighting their foolishness and poor decision-making.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 32:29 express a wish for the people to do?
options: To be wise, understand, and consider their latter end
questions.correctAnswer: To be wise, understand, and consider their latter end
questions.explanation: Verse 29 expresses a desire that the people would gain wisdom and understanding and reflect on their future consequences, urging repentance and obedience.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:30-31, what is the reason one nation can defeat many?
options: Because their Rock sold them and the LORD shut them up
questions.correctAnswer: Because their Rock sold them and the LORD shut them up
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 explain that victory depends on God, the Rock. If God allows defeat, it is because He has sold them and shut them up, not because of their enemies' strength.

questions.question: What image does Deuteronomy 32:32 use to describe the enemies' vine and grapes?
options: Vine of Sodom and fields of Gomorrah, grapes of gall and bitter clusters
questions.correctAnswer: Vine of Sodom and fields of Gomorrah, grapes of gall and bitter clusters
questions.explanation: Verse 32 uses the imagery of Sodom and Gomorrah's wickedness to describe the enemies' vine and grapes as bitter and poisonous, symbolizing their corrupt nature.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:33 describe the enemies' wine?
options: Poison of dragons and cruel venom of asps
questions.correctAnswer: Poison of dragons and cruel venom of asps
questions.explanation: Verse 33 portrays the enemies' wine as deadly poison, emphasizing the danger and evil associated with them.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 32:35 say belongs to the LORD and what will happen in due time?
options: Mercy and blessings; prosperity will come
Vengeance and recompense; their foot shall slide
Peace and joy; enemies will reconcile
Wisdom and understanding; their power will increase
questions.correctAnswer: Vengeance and recompense; their foot shall slide
questions.explanation: Verse 35 declares that vengeance and recompense belong to the LORD and their calamity is imminent, symbolized by their foot sliding at the appointed time.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:36, when will the LORD repent himself for his servants?
options: When their power is gone and none is left shut up
questions.correctAnswer: When their power is gone and none is left shut up
questions.explanation: Verse 36 says the LORD will judge His people and repent for His servants when their power is broken and none are left confined, indicating divine compassion after judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 32:34 indicates that the judgment and vengeance against the enemies is a secret not known to the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 34 states that judgment and vengeance are 'laid up in store' and 'sealed up among my treasures' with the LORD, indicating He is fully aware and in control.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 32 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 32.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 32:39, God declares His exclusive power. Which of the following statements summarizes this declaration?
options: There are many gods but I am the strongest
I kill and make alive; no one can deliver from my hand
God is one among many gods who rule the earth
I only heal but do not judge
questions.correctAnswer: I kill and make alive; no one can deliver from my hand
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:39 states, 'See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.' This emphasizes God's unique sovereign power. This theme echoes in 1 Samuel 2:6, where God's sovereignty over life and death is also declared.

questions.question: What does God say He will do with His 'glittering sword' according to Deuteronomy 32:41?
options: Use it to protect Israel from enemies
Render vengeance to His enemies and reward those who hate Him
Sharpen it for show but not use it
Give it to Moses to lead the people
questions.correctAnswer: Render vengeance to His enemies and reward those who hate Him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:41 states, 'If I whet my glittering sword... I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.' This highlights God's judgment and retribution upon His adversaries. This concept of divine vengeance is also seen in Romans 12:19, which instructs believers to leave vengeance to God.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:43, what is the reason for the nations to rejoice with God's people?
options: Because they will inherit the land with Israel
Because God will avenge the blood of His servants and show mercy to His people
Because the nations will become greater than Israel
Because the nations will be free from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Because God will avenge the blood of His servants and show mercy to His people
questions.explanation: Verse 43 says, 'Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants... and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.' This expresses both judgment against enemies and mercy for Israel. This theme is reflected in Revelation 6:10 where the avenging of God's servants is anticipated.

questions.question: Who accompanied Moses when he spoke the words of the song in Deuteronomy 32:44?
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua (Hoshea) the son of Nun
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:44 states, 'And Moses came and spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he, and Hoshea the son of Nun.' Hoshea is the original name of Joshua, who succeeded Moses. This is consistent with Joshua 1:1-2 where Joshua is appointed leader.

questions.question: What instruction does Moses give to Israel in Deuteronomy 32:46 regarding the words he testified?
options: Ignore them because they are old
Set their hearts to observe and teach their children these words
Only priests should obey these words
Forget these words after crossing Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: Set their hearts to observe and teach their children these words
questions.explanation: Verse 46 commands, 'Set your hearts unto all the words... which ye shall command your children to observe to do.' This stresses the importance of generational faithfulness, a key theme also found in Psalm 78:5-6.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:47, why is the law not a 'vain thing' for the people?
options: Because it is difficult to follow
Because it is their life and will prolong their days in the land
Because it is written by Moses
Because it guarantees wealth and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Because it is their life and will prolong their days in the land
questions.explanation: Verse 47 says, 'For it is not a vain thing for you; because it is your life: and through this thing ye shall prolong your days in the land.' The law is life-giving and crucial for Israel’s longevity in the promised land, a concept also taught in Leviticus 18:5.

questions.question: What mountain was Moses commanded to ascend in Deuteronomy 32:49, and what was he to see from there?
options: Mount Nebo; the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Nebo; the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:49 commands Moses to 'Get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo... and behold the land of Canaan.' This mountain overlooks the promised land, a significant moment also recounted in Numbers 27:12-14.

questions.question: Why was Moses not allowed to enter the promised land according to Deuteronomy 32:51?
options: Because he disobeyed God at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh
Because he was too old to lead
Because he wanted Joshua to lead instead
Because the people rebelled against him
questions.correctAnswer: Because he disobeyed God at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh
questions.explanation: Verse 51 says, 'Because ye trespassed against me... at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh... because ye sanctified me not.' This refers to Moses’ disobedience in Numbers 20:7-12, which caused him to be barred from entering the land.

questions.question: What is the significance of the word 'Rock' as used repeatedly in Deuteronomy 32, especially in verses 4 and 18?
options: It refers to a mountain where Israel camped
It is a metaphor for God's strength, faithfulness, and protection
It represents the physical tablets of the law
It is a symbol of Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It is a metaphor for God's strength, faithfulness, and protection
questions.explanation: Verses like 32:4 and 32:18 use 'Rock' to describe God's perfect work and origin of Israel. The Hebrew word 'Tsur' signifies a strong, unchanging foundation, symbolizing God's reliability. This metaphor is echoed in Psalm 18:2.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used throughout Deuteronomy 32, especially in the structure of the song Moses recites?
options: Parable, a short story with moral
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus, a symmetrical literary structure
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32 is a classic example of chiasm, where ideas are mirrored around a central point, enhancing memorability and emphasizing theological themes. Scholars like Robert Alter note this pattern in the song’s composition.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:37-38 challenge the reliability of idols in contrast to the LORD?
options: By affirming idols can help in times of trouble
By mocking the gods for failing to protect those who trust them
By suggesting idols are more powerful than God
questions.correctAnswer: By mocking the gods for failing to protect those who trust them
questions.explanation: Verses 37-38 question 'Where are their gods... let them rise up and help you,' highlighting the impotence of idols compared to God's power. This critical stance against idolatry is paralleled in Isaiah 46:5-7.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'jealousy' in Deuteronomy 32:21 most closely mean in the original context?
options: God's protective zeal for His covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: God's protective zeal for His covenant people
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'qanna' used in verse 21 conveys a fervent, protective jealousy, reflecting God's passionate commitment to Israel, not human envy. This is consistent with Exodus 20:5 where God is described as a 'jealous God' protecting His covenant.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:35, what does God claim belongs to Him, and what does this imply about His role?
options: Salvation; He saves all who call upon Him
Revenge and recompense; God is the ultimate judge
Peace; God is a bringer of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Revenge and recompense; God is the ultimate judge
questions.explanation: Verse 35 states, 'To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence,' indicating God’s exclusive right to judge and punish wrongdoers. This theme is also found in Nahum 1:2.

questions.question: What historical event is referenced as the reason for Moses’ death outside the promised land in Deuteronomy 32:51-52?
options: The rebellion at Kadesh where Moses struck the rock
The crossing of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: The rebellion at Kadesh where Moses struck the rock
questions.explanation: Verses 51-52 point to the trespass at Meribah-Kadesh where Moses failed to sanctify God by striking the rock (Numbers 20:7-12), resulting in his prohibition from entering the land.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:30 illustrate the consequence of Israel’s reliance on their own strength rather than God?
options: They will conquer easily without help
Their enemies will chase them and put them to flight
They will gain wealth and power
They will become a mighty nation
questions.correctAnswer: Their enemies will chase them and put them to flight
questions.explanation: Verse 30 asks, 'How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them?' showing that defeat comes when God withdraws His protection. This is echoed in Judges 7:2-3 where God’s favor determines victory.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 32 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 32 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Deuteronomy 32:4 when He is described as 'the Rock' whose work is perfect and whose ways are judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: God's immutability and justice
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:4 describes God as a Rock with perfect work and judgment, emphasizing His unchanging nature and just ways, reflecting His immutability and justice.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:8, how did God determine the boundaries of the nations?
options: According to the number of the angels
According to the number of the children of Israel
Based on the size of the land
questions.correctAnswer: According to the number of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:8 states that when God divided the nations, He set the bounds according to the number of the children of Israel, highlighting Israel's unique role in God's plan.

questions.question: What does the imagery of an eagle stirring up her nest and bearing her young on her wings in Deuteronomy 32:11 symbolize about God's relationship with Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection and nurturing care
questions.explanation: In Deuteronomy 32:11, the eagle’s care for her young illustrates God’s protective and nurturing care over Israel, showing His tender guidance.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Deuteronomy 32:15 where Jeshurun waxed fat and forsook God who made him?
options: The doctrine of apostasy and human rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of apostasy and human rebellion
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:15 shows Israel’s rebellion and apostasy after receiving blessings, illustrating human tendency to forsake God despite His providence.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:18 reveal the spiritual condition of Israel in relation to their Creator?
options: They were unmindful and forgot God
questions.correctAnswer: They were unmindful and forgot God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:18 explicitly states that Israel was unmindful of the Rock that begat them and had forgotten God who formed them, highlighting their spiritual neglect.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Deuteronomy 32:19 and 32:20 convey about God's response to Israel's provocation and faithlessness?
options: God ignores their sin and continues blessing them
God abhors their provocation and hides His face to test them
questions.correctAnswer: God abhors their provocation and hides His face to test them
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 20 together teach that God abhors Israel’s provoking sins and responds by hiding His face, allowing consequences to unfold as a test for their faith.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is prominently displayed in Deuteronomy 32:39 where God declares 'I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal'?
options: God's sovereignty over life and death
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over life and death
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:39 reveals God's sovereign power over life and death, showing that He alone controls ultimate fate and healing.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 32:47 describe the importance of the law for Israel's life and longevity in the land?
options: The law is a burdensome obligation
The law is irrelevant to their well-being
The law is their life and a means to prolong days in the land
The law is for priests only
questions.correctAnswer: The law is their life and a means to prolong days in the land
questions.explanation: Verse 47 teaches that the law is vital for Israel’s life and that obedience to it leads to prolonged days in the promised land, emphasizing sanctification and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Deuteronomy 32:49-50 make regarding Moses' death and the promise of the land?
options: Moses will enter and possess the land
Moses will die before entering the land but will see it from afar
Moses will lead the people into exile
Moses will be forgotten after death
questions.correctAnswer: Moses will die before entering the land but will see it from afar
questions.explanation: These verses show the fulfillment of God's judgment on Moses for prior disobedience, fitting the redemptive narrative where Moses views but does not enter the promised land.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Deuteronomy 32:27 provide to skeptics who claim that God does not directly act in history?
options: God's actions are hidden and unknowable
God refrains from judgment to avoid conflict
God fears human wrath and therefore acts indirectly
God’s judgments are evident, but He restrains them to avoid enemy arrogance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgments are evident, but He restrains them to avoid enemy arrogance
questions.explanation: Verse 27 explains that God restrains complete destruction to prevent Israel’s enemies from arrogantly claiming their success was by human power, defending God's active role in history.

questions.question: What does the comparison of Israel's enemies' vine to that of Sodom and Gomorrah in Deuteronomy 32:32 signify?
questions.correctAnswer: Their spiritual barrenness and corruption
questions.explanation: The vine of Sodom and Gomorrah symbolizes corruption and judgment, so this metaphor in verse 32 shows the spiritual corruption of Israel’s enemies.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 32:36, what triggers the Lord to 'repent himself for his servants' and judge His people?
options: When their power is gone and none remain shut up or left
When they prosper and are faithful
questions.correctAnswer: When their power is gone and none remain shut up or left
questions.explanation: Verse 36 teaches that God judges His people and shows compassion when their power collapses and they are thoroughly humbled, highlighting divine discipline and mercy.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine is conveyed by combining Deuteronomy 32:21 (God's jealousy provoked by idols) and 32:41 (God's vengeance upon enemies)?
options: God tolerates idolatry but punishes enemies
God is jealous and will vindicate His honor by judging idolaters and enemies
God's vengeance is unrelated to idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: God is jealous and will vindicate His honor by judging idolaters and enemies
questions.explanation: These verses together teach that God's jealousy is provoked by idolatry, and He will enact vengeance to vindicate His honor against idolaters and adversaries.

questions.question: How do Deuteronomy 32:13-14 and 32:15 together illustrate the theme of blessing and human ingratitude?
options: Israel received abundant blessings but became fat and forsook God
questions.correctAnswer: Israel received abundant blessings but became fat and forsook God
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 describe God's blessings of abundance, while verse 15 shows Israel’s ingratitude by forsaking God, illustrating the theme of human rebellion despite divine provision.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 32:43 teach about God's justice and mercy toward His people and their adversaries?
options: God ignores the blood of His servants
God will avenge His servants and be merciful to His land and people
God shows mercy only to nations
questions.correctAnswer: God will avenge His servants and be merciful to His land and people
questions.explanation: Verse 43 affirms that God enacts justice by avenging the blood of His servants, rewarding adversaries, and showing mercy to His land and people, balancing judgment and grace.
